issues.kind: TWO READINGS (law 1 (2)-(5), law 2 (a), law 3; item 101 R2)
issues.claim: §7.1's outcome table, 'the one home of every ... bend cause of a dry run' (base l. 11285), states a hand stretch's outcome in its `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l. 11343) narrower than the laws at three places. (1) 'a gate it makes for a ground way inside the under-deck strip moved along that way clear of it (none that stands under an aqueduct's arch in an over crossing whose spans clear it, law 1 (5))': law 1 (5) (l. 2724-2725) admits a footprint in an aqueduct's over crossing wherever 'every span over it clears its top', and the strip is the deck's plan widened by stripMarginM while a span's strip is without that margin (l. 2614-2617), so a footprint beside the deck in the margin lies under no span and is admitted; law 2 (a) (l. 2810-2813) and law 3 (l. 2848-2850: 'a gate the op's own wall lays on a standing way, along that way') take the nearest such point; W2's last column (l. 3341, adjudication-r7w M1), the bent-group sentence's (iv) and *No gate and no tower* (l. 3137-3146, 3206-3209), and §7.1's own placed/slid-gate and ground-way-gate clauses (l. 11343, 11345) all say 'the nearest point the laws admit'. Case: a hand drawWall across a standing aqueduct, channel above the wall's top (over); a ground way crossing under a span meets the new trace under that span's deck; the soffit clears the wall's top but not the gatehouse's: the laws move the gate along the way until its footprint leaves the deck's plan (still in the strip's margin); §7.1 carries it a further stripMarginM (1 m as shipped, V11 l. 863) clear of the strip and bends the stretch through the farther gate. Two builders, two maps from one gesture; the §7.1 build passes a nearer lawful place, the outcome Part P pass 8 ruled against item 101 R2 as the program reads it (PRB7H-LCK-03, adjudication-r7.md l. 3990) and adjudication-r7v graded major in this row (VF7-HND-01, l. 78; famverify-hand-r7.md l. 95 judged this clause 'conformed'). No bar holds it: T110-2 (4) (l. 19402-19404) asserts 'laid clear of the under-deck strip, or under an aqueduct's arch that clears it' on fixtures whose stated geometry does not put a ground way's crossing under a span that fails to clear the gate, so S0 (l. 19256-19263) cannot make it assert the laws' place, and a build of §7.1's row passes every bar. (2) The same row names a road deck's lawful crossing 'under a road deck's span or beyond its foot', where law 1 (3) (l. 2716-2720) builds the band through supports, the bent-group sentence's lawful crossing (l. 3184) is 'under its span or at its support' and T110-2 (4) was rewritten 'under the deck's first span or at a support clear of the ramp' (l. 19416-19417; adjudication-r7w S1: 'naming the span alone would pin a form the laws choose'). (3) It names an aqueduct's over crossing 'under a span that clears the wall's top and never through a standing support', omitting the cleared support's ring where every span above the band, standing or fallen, clears its top (law 1 (2), l. 2707-2709; examples l. 3061-3063, 3180-3182; a cleared ring is no span's strip, l. 2616). Each restates the laws narrower than they are; place (1) alone grades the finding major, (2) and (3) are the same row's same defect.
issues.required_change: 1. §7.1's outcome table, the `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (base l. 11343), its outcome: "an unlawful crossing moved to the nearest lawful one (an aqueduct's deck line crossed once in the form its level there gives — over, under a span that clears the wall's top and never through a standing support, where its channel runs above that top; merged where it runs within the wall's height —, law 1 (2); under a road deck's span or beyond its foot through a gate there, whichever law 3 finds nearer)" → "an unlawful crossing moved to the nearest lawful one (an aqueduct's deck line crossed once in the form its level there gives — over, under a span that clears the wall's top or through a `cleared` support's ring where every span above the band, standing or fallen, clears that top, never through a standing support, where its channel runs above that top; merged where it runs within the wall's height —, law 1 (2); a road deck's under a span or at a support, the band laid through it, or beyond its foot through a gate there, whichever law 3 finds nearer, law 1 (3), (4); its worked example the bent-group sentence's lawful crossing and (i))". 2. The same row, its outcome: "a gate it makes for a ground way inside the under-deck strip moved along that way clear of it (none that stands under an aqueduct's arch in an over crossing whose spans clear it, law 1 (5))" → "a gate it makes for a ground way where §2.7's laws bar one there (law 1 (5)) moved along that way to the nearest point at which they admit its footprint (law 2 (a), law 3: in an aqueduct's over crossing it may lie inside the under-deck strip, under no span that fails to clear it; its worked example the crossing table's row W2)". 3. END at scope, §13.2's T110-2 (4) (l. 19402-19404): "a gate the wall makes for a ground way laid clear of the under-deck strip, or under an aqueduct's arch that clears it (§2.7's laws, law 1 (5), law 2 (a))" → "a gate the wall makes for a ground way laid at the nearest point along that way at which §2.7's laws admit its footprint (§2.7's laws, law 1 (5), law 2 (a), law 3) — and, on a run of the hand `drawWall` across the standing aqueduct whose seed is searched so that a ground way crossing under a span over level ground meets the new trace under that span's deck, the channel there above the wall's top and the span's soffit clearing the wall's top but not the gatehouse's, that gate moved along the way only until its footprint leaves the deck's plan, the footprint still meeting the under-deck strip beside the deck, the stretch bent through it, part of its bend —".

issues.kind: CATALOGUE (two family bends whose line no form words)
issues.claim: V09's lines take their form 'by what was drawn or moved' (V09 l. 2104) or 'by what was edited' (l. 2102). (a) `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'s crossing form is 'for a crossing moved along {way} to the nearest lawful one (under an arch that clears the wall, or beyond a road deck's foot through a gate there)' (V09 l. 2104): a crossing bent from a road deck's ramp to the deck's first lawful crossing (bent-group (i), base l. 3197-3202; T110-2 (4) l. 19413-19418) and an aqueduct crossing moved to a nearer merged crossing by its level (law 1 (2), law 3; adjudication-r7w class member C1) are neither, so one builder words them in this form and another in the keep-clear form. (b) A raised or aqueduct stroke whose strip would hold a standing wall's band without crossing its line is barred by law 1 (4) (l. 2721-2723) and bent off by law 2 (a), law 3 under §7.1's catch-all key `bend.raised.wall` (l. 11346); `bend.raised.wall`'s forms (V09 l. 2102: down before a wall, a re-shape stopped short, a measure bent) and `bend.wall.aqueductArch`'s (l. 2103: over, merged) word none of it. The outcome is the laws' in every build; only the words differ (VF7-HND-03's and VF7v-HND-05's class): minor.
issues.required_change: 1. V09 §4.9's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` (V09 l. 2104), its line cell: "for a crossing moved along {way} to the nearest lawful one (under an arch that clears the wall, or beyond a road deck's foot through a gate there)" → "for a crossing moved along {way} to the nearest lawful one (§2.7's laws, law 1 (2)–(4), law 3; its worked example the bent-group sentence (i))". 2. V09 §4.9's `bend.raised.wall` (V09 l. 2102), its line cell: after "for its Arch spacing, Deck height or width bent to the nearest lawful value, "{way}'s {measure} is {v}, the nearest that {wall} allows."" add " — and, for a raised or aqueduct stroke bent off a wall whose band its strip would hold without crossing its line, "{way} keeps clear of {wall}, {m} m off your line.""; its source cell: after "(§2.7's laws, law 2 (a), law 3; its worked example the crossing table's C13)" add "; a raised or aqueduct stroke bent off a wall it would run along (§2.7's laws, law 1 (4), law 2 (a), law 3)".

issues.kind: READERS ('held or not' without J147's axis; VF7v-HND-03's class)
issues.claim: VF7v-HND-03's fix wrote V09 §4.20.2 (4) 'an aqueduct drawn across a standing wall, placement-locked or not, crosses it' (V09 l. 3019); the catalogue row naming the same bend keeps, in its source cell, 'file f item 363: an aqueduct drawn across a standing wall, held or not' (`bend.wall.aqueductArch`, V09 l. 2103), whose second form is 'The wall is built up round the aqueduct'. Read with J147's *held* (base l. 2653-2656) it merges into a shape-locked wall, which law 1 (10) bars (l. 2741-2743); the cell cites (10) and no hand op makes a shape lock before round 8, so nothing built or tested changes: minor, the sixth site of VF7v-HND-03's class (R7-01 (2)'s sweep missed it).
issues.required_change: V09 §4.9's `bend.wall.aqueductArch` (V09 l. 2103), its source cell: "an aqueduct drawn across a standing wall, held or not" → "an aqueduct drawn across a standing wall, placement-locked or not, a shape-locked one never merged into".

issues.kind: TESTS (two bars gloss a gate's lawful places in an aqueduct's strip as 'clear of the strip' or 'under an arch')
issues.claim: Law 1 (5) admits a gate's footprint in an aqueduct's over crossing wherever no span over it fails to clear its top, beside the deck in the strip's margin among those places (VF7w-HND-01, place 1). T110-2 (4) glosses the placed gate's nearest lawful place as '(§2.7's laws, law 1 (5): clear of the strip, or under an aqueduct's arch that clears it)' (base l. 19430-19431), and T-V9-52 has a road under an arch that 'clears the wall but not the gate's top — crosses it clear of the strip' (V09 l. 4428), where §7.1's row (l. 11345) and row (b) (l. 2914) give the nearest crossing at which the laws admit the gate, which may leave its footprint in the margin. T110-2's lead (S0, l. 19256-19263) makes each bar assert the laws' outcome where its words differ, so no correct build fails: minor, the words conformed.
issues.required_change: 1. §13.2's T110-2 (4) (base l. 19430-19431): "(§2.7's laws, law 1 (5): clear of the strip, or under an aqueduct's arch that clears it)" → "(§2.7's laws, law 1 (5): clear of the strip, or, in an aqueduct's over crossing, where no span over it fails to clear it)". 2. END at V09, T-V9-52 (V09 l. 4428): "— crosses it clear of the strip, with `bend.raised.underSpan` in its wall form," → "— crosses it at the nearest point at which §2.7's laws admit its gate (law 1 (5), law 2 (a), law 3; clear of the strip on the merged variant), with `bend.raised.underSpan` in its wall form,".
